transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions! First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week from your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month. So gentle gardening is fine, but avoid anything too demanding.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do! When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you don't have any left, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, thanks for clarifying. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Some light sensitivity is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Some light sensitivity is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details, so I'm not sure exactly how long ago your surgery was. If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thanks again!

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting "Some light sensitivity is quite normal...". However, the `escalation_criteria` point was not conveyed at all, as the agent was interrupted before it could deliver the full message regarding significant pain or severe sensitivity with a red and painful eye.
